elements.label: Figure 6.2
elements.description:
Horizontal grouped bar chart titled "Top three reasons why conditions are same or worse than five years ago". X-axis: "Share of affected households (%)", scale 0 to 60 with gridlines at 0, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. Legend: 2020 (teal), 2018 (orange), 2010 (gray). No values are printed on the bars, so the following are approximate readings (~):

- Accident or disaster (non-environment): 2020 ~2; 2018 ~3; 2010 ~5
- Decreased land use: 2020 ~1; 2018 ~2; 2010 ~3
- Family or friend conflicts: 2020 ~19; 2018 ~19; 2010 ~20
- Job loss or underemployment: 2020 ~42; 2018 ~38; 2010 ~42
- Low income: 2020 ~52; 2018 ~50; 2010 ~47
- High prices of consumer goods: 2020 ~27; 2018 ~23; 2010 ~27
- Illness or death in the family: 2020 ~29; 2018 ~33; 2010 ~29
- Natural disaster impacting agriculture: 2020 ~6; 2018 ~6; 2010 ~7
- Cattle and poultry disease: 2020 ~11; 2018 ~13; 2010 ~10
- Low selling prices of agricultural products: 2020 ~11; 2018 ~15; 2010 ~10
- Increased costs of agricultural production: 2020 ~36; 2018 ~37; 2010 ~39

Note printed below the chart: "Not all households selected 3 reasons. Agriculture includes forestry and aquaculture." Source: World Bank staff calculations using VHLSS.

Pattern: low income is the most cited reason in all three years, and most agriculture-related reasons are cited more often in 2018 and 2010 than in 2020, while job loss and low income are the highest-share reasons overall.
